corrected_value.title_o: Hot under the collar in a lukewarm environment: Words associated with hot temperature increase aggressive thoughts and hostile perceptions

decisions.quote: This is a direct replication of DeWall and Bushman's (2009) study demonstrating that priming participants with heat-related constructs increases perceptions of hostility relative to participants primed with either cold-related constructs or neutral constructs.
decisions.location: Summary / Overview (line 3) and Research question and hypotheses (lines 16-17)
decisions.reason: The primary OSF registration text explicitly identifies the target as Experiment 2 of DeWall & Bushman (2009), a two-study paper testing whether heat-related primes increase aggressive thoughts and hostile perceptions/attributions relative to cold or neutral primes. This uniquely matches the shipped original (DeWall & Bushman, 2009, DOI 10.1016/j.jesp.2009.05.003) and pairs with blind target_index 0 (which omitted title and DOI only because the registration lacks a formal reference list).

decisions.quote:
item33: informative failure to replicate
item34: Despite having sufficient statistical power and closely following the methods, I failed to find any effect of heat priming on hostile perceptions.
decisions.reason: Across two new samples (Study 1: d = -0.12 and d = -0.02; Study 2: d = -0.06 and d = 0.00), the author explicitly concludes that the replication was an 'informative failure to replicate' and failed to find any effect of heat priming on hostile perceptions despite sufficient statistical power. Although the shipped quote came from the corresponding manuscript phrasing rather than the registration fields, both shipped and blind codings agree on the 'failed' outcome.

decisions.quote: The current study is a direct replication of Experiment 2 of DeWall & Bushman (2009). This replication study will use the exact same study materials as the original study.
decisions.location: Research question and hypotheses (line 17) and Post-Completion registration responses (line 6)
decisions.reason: The study collected new data across two independent samples (Study 1 and Study 2) using the original materials to re-test Experiment 2 of DeWall & Bushman (2009), making it a replication.

decisions.quote:
DeWall and Bushman (2009) conducted 2 studies demonstrating that priming participants with heat-related concepts increased the accessibility of aggressive thoughts and hostile attributions relative to participants primed with cold-related concepts or neutral concepts. 
The current study is a direct replication of Experiment 2 of DeWall & Bushman (2009). This replication study will use the exact same study materials as the original study.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. The blind coder extracted 'DeWall & Bushman' (2009) without a title or DOI because the OSF registration text cites it in-text without a formal reference entry. However, the source text explicitly identifies this target as the 2009 two-study paper by DeWall and Bushman showing that priming participants with heat-related concepts increases aggressive thoughts and hostile perceptions/attributions relative to cold or neutral primes (lines 3, 16-19). That exact study is already represented in shipped row 1552 (C. Nathan DeWall & Brad J. Bushman, 2009, 'Hot under the collar in a lukewarm environment: Words associated with hot temperature increase aggressive thoughts and hostile perceptions', 10.1016/j.jesp.2009.05.003).
